patches.what: `inert` passed through a spread, as an empty string when collapsed
patches.reason: Upstream writes `inert={!isExpanded}`, which React 19 types accept and React 18 types do not, and which React 18 also warns about at runtime because it is not a boolean attribute. The site typechecks and runs on React 18 (the same version the app uses), so the attribute is spread in as `inert=""`: the DOM gets exactly the same attribute, the collapsed panel stays out of the tab order and the accessibility tree, and nothing is logged.

patches.what: vendored from card-18, the published name of the same block
patches.reason: @shadcn-space/card-21 is only served by shadcnspace.com, which is unreachable here, and its source is not in the project's public repo (card-18 is, in the same folder, with the same layout and the same default rows). card-21 is that file with the copy updated, so this is the published bytes rather than a guess.

The upstream block hard-codes "Others tools", the vendor's own name and its badge. Naming the columns is what lets the same block compare ResearchEngine against subscription research apps, which is the job it was picked for; the defaults still render upstream's own comparison.
The registry serves the file with CRLF; this repository keeps text files LF so diffs stay readable.

upstream.note: The embla-backed carousel Aceternity's registry installs as components/ui/carousel.tsx (their image and card carousels both import it). ui.aceternity.com is unreachable from this machine, so the file comes from a public MIT checkout of the same component.

patches.what: the two arrow buttons are plain buttons, not the shadcn Button primitive
patches.reason: This site's button component is a link (`ButtonLink`, an anchor, because every button on the page goes somewhere). The carousel's arrows are controls, not links, so they carry the same classes on a real <button> with an aria-label each.
A gallery has to open on the picture that was clicked. Aceternity's own carousel exposes this prop; the vendored copy did not, so it is added here and used by the screenshot gallery.

patches.what: colour tokens mapped onto this site's palette
patches.reason: `bg-background` / `border-input` / `bg-accent` are shadcn tokens this site does not define (an undefined colour variable renders transparent with no error, which is how the app's search box once became invisible). The buttons use the site's own surface, border and foreground variables.

patches.what: quote style and semicolons normalised to this repository's formatting
patches.reason: Cosmetic only: the site is formatted with single quotes and no semicolons, so the file is not re-formatted by every later pass through a formatter.

upstream.note: Aceternity's typewriter effect, from a public MIT checkout (the registry host is unreachable here). It draws the answer in the 'ask it something' animation.

patches.what: character and cursor colours are this site's tokens
patches.reason: Upstream paints characters `dark:text-white text-black` and the cursor `bg-blue-500`. Mapped onto `text-foreground` and `bg-brand` so the animation belongs to the page palette instead of shipping a second blue.

upstream.note: `@aceternity/features-section-demo-3`: the four-cell bento grid (6-column layout, hairline dividers, copy above the picture). From a public MIT checkout, because ui.aceternity.com is unreachable from this machine.

patches.what: the demo's own copy, photographs and globe are removed; the grid takes its cells as a prop
patches.reason: Upstream hard-codes its demo: a heading about thousands of features, five Unsplash photographs, a YouTube thumbnail and a cobe globe. None of that is this product, and stock art on a page about a local-first app is exactly the tell the round asked to remove. The structure - the unequal cells, the dividers, the title-then-picture rhythm - is kept and fed this app's own four stories and screenshots.

patches.what: the `cobe` dependency is dropped with the globe
patches.reason: Removing the globe removes the only reason the demo had a WebGL dependency, so this site does not install cobe at all.
`dark:border-neutral-800`, `text-white` and `text-neutral-300` became the site's border, foreground and muted variables, so the bento follows one palette with the rest of the page.
